# Health savings account

## Summary

English Wikipedia article on health savings accounts: tax-advantaged accounts open only to people covered by a high-deductible plan. The points that mattered to us: the money belongs to the account holder, not the employer; unspent balances carry over every year rather than expiring; and the account is distinct from employer-owned reimbursement arrangements.

## Why It Matters

Two of our decisions rest on the ownership and carry-over points. In 2025 they made the HDHP more attractive ([[health-plan-decision-2025-11-10]]). In 2026 they meant leaving the HDHP did not cost us the balance: the account stays open and invested even though we can no longer contribute ([[open-enrollment-review-2026-10-21]], [[how-should-we-invest-the-hsa]]).

## Key Details

- Eligibility to contribute depends on being on a qualifying plan; eligibility to spend does not.
- Contrasted with flexible spending accounts, which do not roll over in the same way.

## Caveats

Contribution limits and tax rules in the article are for one country's system. Our administrator's rules ([[hsa-account-summary-2026-10]]) and [[imogen-park]] are the authority for us.
